blocks.text: For Laura Gonzalez, Chief Financial Officer. From Rachel Brown, Vice President, with Mark Allen, Partner. Confidential; prepared for the company's deal team and its counsel, and not for wider circulation.

This period was about turning agreed terms into signed paper, so what we needed from you was mostly decisions. We put three questions to you. Two are settled. On the working capital target, you and the shareholders accepted the buyer's figure in return for a lower cap on the indemnity. The buyer took that trade and did not reopen anything else to get it. On the customer contracts that carry change-of-control language, you chose to approach those customers before signing. We agree with that choice, and we have planned the remaining weeks around it. The third question is still open. The buyer wants the continuing shareholders to execute their employment agreements at signing; we had proposed that they sign at closing. Either can be made to work, and we would not spend goodwill on it. The drafting differs, though, and the purchase agreement cannot go back to the buyer's counsel until we know which one you want.

items: Confirmatory diligence. The buyer's accountants and counsel have closed their request lists. The last questions, on revenue recognition, were answered from the model, and every figure we gave them ties back to it.

Working capital. We rebuilt the monthly working capital schedule on the buyer's definitions. That is what let you settle the target question with confidence, and it gives us the base for the closing estimate.
Purchase agreement. We have taken the draft through two full turns with your counsel. Every business point is now agreed except the employment agreement timing described above.

Valuation support. We refreshed our analysis of {{fact:f:E-2014-001.comparators}} for the latest trailing results and sent it to the shareholders, so the board's view of the price rests on current numbers.

Marketing record. The marketing phase is closed and documented. For the file, it ended with {{fact:f:E-2014-001.pipeline-buyers-contacted}}, {{fact:f:E-2014-001.pipeline-ndas-executed}} and {{fact:f:E-2014-001.pipeline-indications-received}}. Each party that did not go forward has had a letter from us thanking them and reminding them of their confidentiality obligations.

Consents list. We compiled the contracts, leases and permits that need consent or notice on a change of control. Your counsel has confirmed the list, and the customer contracts on it are the ones you have chosen to raise before signing.
Customer approach. Mark Allen agreed the outline of the customer conversations with you, including what may and may not be said about the buyer before the agreement is signed.
Customer conversations. Mark Allen will join you on the customer calls in the coming week. We will send you a short note after each one.
Employment agreements. Drafts for the continuing shareholders are with your counsel. They are on hold until the timing question is answered.

Disclosure schedules. Your team is assembling the schedules with our help. We are reading each one against the representation it supports, because that is the first thing the buyer's counsel will do, and we would like to find any gap before they do.
Funds flow. We have opened the funds flow memorandum with both sets of counsel. It cannot be final until the closing working capital estimate is agreed.

Process file. We are putting together the record of the sale for your files: the approved buyer list ({{fact:f:E-2014-001.scope}}), the executed confidentiality agreements, and our correspondence with each party.
Closing checklist. We keep the checklist jointly with your counsel and circulate it each Monday. Anything that slips will show there first, with a name against it.

blocks.text: Signing now depends on three things, and the order matters. Your answer on the employment agreements comes first, because the next draft of the purchase agreement waits on it. The customer conversations come second. If any customer asks for more than a courtesy call, we will tell you the same day and talk it through with you before anything is offered. The closing working capital estimate comes last. With the target settled, that is now a matter of arithmetic between the two sets of accountants. The risk we are watching is time. The longer the agreement stays unsigned, the more of the buyer's attention drifts back to monthly results, and the next close will reach their accountants on its usual schedule whether we are ready or not. We see no change to the budget. The remaining work sits within the engagement fee of {{fact:f:E-2014-001.fee}} set out in our engagement letter, and we do not expect to come back to you on expenses. We expect this to be our last report of this kind before signing. The one thing we need from you now is your decision on the employment agreement timing, by Tuesday if you can, so that the draft goes back to the buyer's counsel before the week is out.
